'''Wolfgang Heinrich Johannes Fuchs''' (May 19, 1915 – February 24, 1997) was a British [[mathematician]] specializing in [[complex analysis]]. His main area of research was [[Nevanlinna theory]].

Fuchs received his [[Ph.D.]] in 1941 from the [[University of Cambridge]], under the direction of [[Albert Ingham]].<ref>{{ cite journal
   | last = Anderson
   | first = J. Milne |author2=Drasin, David |author3=Sons, Linda R.
   | title = Wolfgang Heinrich Johannes Fuchs (1915–1997)
   |date=December 1998
   | journal = [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]
   | volume = 45
   | issue = 11
   | pages =1472–1478
   | url = http://www.ams.org/notices/199811/mem-fuchs.pdf
   | accessdate = 2007-11-27 }}</ref> He joined the faculty of [[Cornell University]] in 1950 and spent the rest of his career there.
